title: Design guide and UI building: changes from your Pages feedback

steps.headline: Already added to the guide today: labels are statements, say it once, one (i) per feature, one box per item.
steps.changed: Four rules from your step 4 notes went in: labels and headings name what is under them, never questions; if two lines say the same thing one goes; how a feature works sits behind one (i) by its title; a single item (a run, a permission) gets its own box.
steps.notice: Every later design reads these before drawing.

steps.headline: Add a rule: every label uses the words a newcomer would say out loud?
steps.today: The guide asks for plain words, sentence case and few words.
steps.problem: Labels still come out as riddles: "On their own", "What it may do", "Money chat". Each was short and in sentence case, so it passed the rules.
steps.proposal: A label names a thing or a state the way someone new would say it ("Paused", "Permissions", the chat's real name). A test: read it with no screen around it; if it needs the screen to make sense, rewrite it.

steps.headline: Add a rule: ✕ only on things that end; a panel that comes back as it was hides instead?
steps.today: The guide says every popup and panel closes with the ✕.
steps.problem: Your step 3 note: on the page chat, "X reads as end chat permanently" when it actually reopens where you left it.
steps.proposal: ✕ for things that end or are thrown away (a popup, a draft). A panel that keeps its place and comes back the same (the page chat) uses a hide button instead.

steps.headline: Add a rule: making something new has one main button and no on/off switches?
steps.today: The guide covers one filled button per view, but nothing on making new things.
steps.problem: New automation shipped first with "Save, turned off" and "Turn on", then a switch in its corner; both read as confusing.
steps.proposal: A create screen has one main action (Create) and no state switches; turning it off or pausing happens after, where the thing lives.

steps.intro: Most of your other notes were "this doesn't look like the rest of the app".

steps.headline: Extend the guide's "which piece for which job" table with whole surfaces, not just buttons and fields?
steps.today: The table names small pieces: a button, a switch, a dropdown. Bigger jobs have no named surface.
steps.problem: Each new screen re-invents bigger things: its own model list instead of the app's model picker, a chat header unlike any other, a page of rows where the Library uses cards, tab strips per permission.
steps.proposal: Add rows for the big jobs, each naming the existing surface to reuse.

options.label: Add the big jobs
options.summary: Pick a model → the model picker; a collection of things → Library cards; one thing's settings → a detail popup like Plugin details; a per-item mode in a list → a pill that opens a small menu; a chat inside a page → the page chat panel; a page with sections → Settings' layout.
pros: The builder looks up the surface before drawing, so it can't invent one.
cons: The table needs a line each time a new surface is approved.

steps.path: The first deck of any new screen
steps.headline: Should the first deck of a new screen show the existing screens it copies, beside it?
steps.today: The rule says to name two or three similar screens. Names go in the text, and you never see the pictures.
steps.problem: Round 1 of Automations named its references, but still drew a list where Your library uses cards. You only found out by reacting to the result.
steps.proposal: The deck builder takes a "references" list and shows those screens' pictures as the deck's first slide, so you and the builder look at the same thing.

options.label: A references slide
pros: You can say "make it more like this one" before any drawing is judged.
The builder has to actually open them.
cons: One more slide to look at.

options.label: Names only
cons: What happened this time keeps happening.

steps.path: The automatic checks run before you see anything
steps.headline: Add an automatic check that flags question-style labels and explanation lines in new screens?
steps.today: Code checks catch hand-made colours and buttons, not words.
steps.problem: Wording is the most common thing you send back, and nothing catches it before you do.
steps.proposal: A check that fails on a label ending in "?" or starting with What / When / How / If, and lists every grey hint line on a new screen for the builder to justify or remove. The outside tester also gets your copy rules as things to flag.

options.label: Check and tester
pros: Catches the common cases automatically; the tester catches the rest.
cons: Now and then it will flag a label that's fine, and the builder will have to mark it OK.

options.label: Tester only
cons: Relies on judgement, which missed it this time.

steps.headline: Every question about how something looks comes with a picture?
steps.problem: "Add a permission" was asked in words and you said it was hard to visualize; drawn the next round, it was easy.
steps.proposal: A question about appearance or layout always has a drawing of each option. Words-only questions are kept for behaviour (what happens, when, what's allowed).

steps.headline: Only offer "pick one" when the options really can't be combined?
steps.today: Several designs of one thing go on one pick-one slide.
steps.problem: Your step 3 note: "why are you offering these to me like they're exclusive options?" — when they could all be had together.
steps.proposal: Before a pick-one slide, the builder checks whether the options combine; if they do, each becomes its own yes/no instead.

steps.headline: Keep one-off builds out of decks about the bigger system?
steps.today: Nothing stops a planning deck from mixing in single features.
steps.problem: Your first Pages note: "we shouldn't be looking at single pages like the home page here. this work is about the broader architecture."
steps.proposal: A deck about a system asks only about the system; one-off builds become their own items.

steps.prompt: Other patterns in your feedback the guide should capture
steps.headline: Anything else from your feedback the guide or the way UI gets built should change?
steps.today: These proposals come from your notes across the Pages decks.
steps.problem: Some feedback may not have been turned into a rule.
steps.proposal: Type anything to add; it becomes a guide rule or a check.
